notes.title: Zoria: Community Translations Added
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Commanders![/h2]

It's been a while, but we have some good news for you! We’re excited to share some fantastic updates with you in our latest [b]Patch 1.1.8[/b], all focused on making Zoria more accessible and enjoyable for players around the world.

We've been asked multiple times if other than English version will be available. Not only that, but we stated a few times, that Zoria is a very complex game with a huge word count, and it might be impossible to implement it budget-wise.

Fortunately, thanks to our great community, we're able to introduce a Community Translation! With this update we're launching [b]French, Italian, German, Spanish[/b] and [b]Russian[/b] localization. Thank you, our fellow community members, for doing a great job with LQA! 

[h3]New Language Versions[/h3]

[b]•   ​Language Selection Panel:​[/b]
You can now easily choose your preferred language directly from the in-game settings menu

[b]•   ​French Community Localization:​[/b]
We’re thrilled to introduce a full French localization, thanks to the incredible efforts of our community translators. Special thank you to:
• [i]Alexandre "​All_zebest​" Mangin[/i] – Localization project manager, translator, and proofreader\
• [i]Philippe "​pendragon64​" Reybaud[/i] – Co-translator, proofreader, and beta tester

[b]•   ​Italian Localization:​[/b]
Italian players can now enjoy Zoria: Age of Shattering in their native language. Special thanks to our proofreaders and testers:
• [i]Rocco Pezzullo (​Freemont​)[/i] and [i]Languagepack.it[/i]

[b]•   ​German Localization:​[/b]
The German version is now available and currently under community review. We appreciate your feedback to help us polish it further!

[b]•   ​Spanish Localization:​[/b]
Spanish localization is also live and under community review. Your input is invaluable as we work to perfect it!

[b]•   ​Russian Localization:​[/b]
Russian localization in our opinion requires the most support due to grammatical structures, we also supported ourselves with machine translation to be able to prepare the base for iterations. We are counting on you to help us make the translation better!

***

[b]A Note on Community Involvement:​[/b]
While we strive for the highest quality, some translations may not be perfect yet. If you spot any errors, have suggestions, or would like to help with proofreading and testing, we warmly invite you to join our dedicated localization channel on Discord! Your contributions make Zoria better for everyone.

[b]Join the Localization Effort:​[/b] [url=https://discord.com/invite/k3fPxX8][b]Discord[/b][/url]
Thank you to everyone who has contributed so far, and to all our players for your ongoing support and feedback!

Have fun playing,

So, without further ado, let's jump into the update. [b]Here are the most significant changes that we implemented since Zoria's launch back in March:[/b]

⚔️ Greatly improved Inventory Management and storage space
- [b]Added individual resources-based inventories[/b] for Consumables, Materials, Ingredients, and Crafting Items to no longer consume inventory space
- Only Weapons, Armors, Trinkets and Blueprints will require inventory slots
- All items can still be sold/traded as well as used everywhere in crafting/combat
- [b]Potions are now sorted by effect and effect magnitude[/b] instead of level

This change offers greater flexibility in avoiding Line-of-Sight issues and generally improves combat experience flow by allowing the use of AP abilities while also moving in the same turn.

notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Commanders![/h2]

We've been reading your suggestions, comments and reviews. Huge thanks to everyone who shared their thoughts with us. This update is huge, really. With that, we hope it covers the most frequent issues and significantly improve your experience with Zoria. Please enjoy!

[h2]Patch 1.0.4[/h2]
[h3]📌 Scene changes [/h3]
Rithvale Area
⚔️ fixed a few environmental issues with floating objects;
⚔️ Ruvan Village Elder NPC renamed to reflect her name;
⚔️ fixed Commoner pathing;
⚔️ disabled warning in the Effigy creature’s area when leaving for Thonargond;
⚔️ graverobbers are now appearing as intended during the quest and not before;
⚔️ Removed the Elder of Ruvan from the day-night timetable, to make her accessible at all times;
⚔️ Update Dragon to level 10 and updated some of its stats to make the fight more relevant.
Rithvale Outpost
⚔️ fixed double Old-Bean Truff NPC.
Rithvale Keep
⚔️ fixed Level 2 upgrade wall that was missing collision;
⚔️ added missing outline to NPC.
Daeg Marastir
⚔️ fixed an issue that was preventing the Combat Tutorial to trigger;
⚔️ streamlined the flow, removed some fights, adjusted damage and hit points for enemies to make the area easier to navigate for new players. 
Yarnigan Mine
⚔️ fixed an edge case where, if you did not deliver “Lost Miners” quest but delivered “Ther Mine” quest you would be locked out of delivering “Lost Miners” as the NPC will disappear. 
Forest of Nurdundas 
⚔️ added a new merchant. 
The Shrieking Pass
⚔️ Gerwin is now properly recruited. 
Bilnaram Hills
⚔️ Added info on the map regarding Wizard being necessary for Bilnaram Cellar 
Thonargond
⚔️ fixed an issue with the dome being accessible in a certain area. 
Grimwood Crypt
⚔️ Improved rooftop hide event near certain buildings. 
Thonargond Citadel, Thonargond Seat of Ancestors 
⚔️ Fixed level of pickup gear recipes from auto Level to Level 14 

[h3]📌 Game-wide changes[/h3] 
⚔️ Increase Physical/Magical Damage Weapon stats for 2 handed items (from 1.5x to 2.5x versus one handed items) 
⚔️ Merchant System – Fixed option to Buy/Sell recipes (gear, cooking, alchemy) 
⚔️ Quest Marks – fixed issue with color of quest mark (yellow instead of blue) when a merchant had also a rumor entry. 
⚔️ Changed default level of audio settings to match the reset values. 
⚔️ World Shrines that buff Stamina will now give the corresponding HP as well. 
⚔️ Added missing Voice Over for Amaldir.
⚔️ Added Priestess of Amaldir world shrines in multiple areas that clear Curses and Diseases. 
⚔️ Multiple typos are fixed in quest entries, UI and game story/lore. 

[h3]📌 Class Changes [/h3]
⚔️ Sentinel Class - increase damage for Backbreaker, Vigilant Strike, Igniting Blade. Banner of Might will give a buff on 20% Intellect as well beside Agility and Strength 
⚔️ Kingsman Class - increased damage for some abilities and increased range for King's Fire ability 
⚔️ Necromancer Class - increased damage and reduced cost for certain abilities. Infernal Edict damage and hit points adjusted 
⚔️ Priest - Healing Well is now placed next in the Combat Queue thus providing the healing effect right after the end of turn of the current Priest character. 

[h3]📌 Combat System [/h3]
⚔️ During exploration Combat Focus will only deplete to a certain level based on the game difficulty (Easy – 35, Normal - 20, Hard – 15, Unfair - 10) 
⚔️ Enemy abilities max range was lowered to values that match the max range of follower abilities 
⚔️ Removed the 4th Action Point bonus for Boss characters when below 30% health (Easy Difficulty). For all other difficulty options elite and boss character will receive the 3rd Action Point respectively the 4th Action Point for at slightly lower health levels. 
⚔️ Attack of Opportunity – increase change of triggering to 30% as well as range of trigger to 5 meters 
⚔️ Greatly improved flow of combat system through the added 7 meters of free movement at the start of the character’s turn. This change offers greater flexibility in avoiding Line-of-Sight issues and generally improves combat experience flow by allowing the use of AP abilities while also moving in the same turn. 
⚔️ Free movement range can be partially expended during the player’s turn over multiple movement actions so long the character still has Action Points left. Each Action Point consumed for movement will increase the free movement range by an additional 7 meters, governed by the same consumption mechanic. 

[b]The changes in this patch make for a comprehensive update to the combat system. This update is intended not only to improve on certain aspects that have been reported but also make the combat flow richer and offer a better experience overall.  [/b]

notes.title: A glimpse into the Enemies in Zoria ⚔
notes.content:
[h2]Commanders![/h2]

Creating the world can be hard and complicated, but fortunately, to us it was also fun 😀 Today we wanted to offer you a glimpse into the [b]creatures you'll surely encounter[/b] while playing Zoria: Age of Shattering. While there is plenty to choose from, with fantasy classics such as skeletons, dragons or ghosts, we picked a bunch that we personally like the most, so it's kind of random 😂

[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [td][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/3a67eb1a74e69e6cdb246246b3068e4df5bdb1cb.png[/img][/td]
        [td]Let's start with the terrifying [b]Cave Claw Crawlers[/b]. As their name suggests, these grotesque creatures dwell in caves and other dark places. Their exoskeleton is a fortress of resilience, blending seamlessly into the darkness, making them masters of stealth and surprise. Armed with large, sharp blades, they are a force to be reckoned with, combining brute force with speed and agility.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/e2931ca688ef15d9f7830eceaef47986f798e8cc.png[/img][/td]
        [td]Next, we have the [b]Water Elementals[/b]. These entities, despite their aquatic namesake, are often found roaming the land. Their origin is a mystery, but it's believed they are born from concentrated magic energy, animating the prevailing element in their vicinity. They are solitary creatures, aggressively engaging in combat when approached. The older they are, the more powerful they become, making every encounter a thrilling challenge.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/fff2ee108cbecba5a65bcdbc9d019a654970c0e1.png[/img][/td]
        [td]Then there are the [b]Gargoyles[/b], magical constructs crafted by the wizards of old. At first glance, they may seem like ordinary statues, but get too close, and their true nature is revealed. These ancient guardians are carved from enchanted stone, and their cold, crystalline eyes gleam with an unnatural glow. They are fiercely loyal to their creators, and in battle, they channel their magical essence into devastating attacks.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/820049187fb01344f03adc28add125821860bd12.png[/img][/td]
        [td]Last but not least, we have the [b]Ancestor Guardians[/b]. These ancient creatures belong to the civilization of the Ancestors. Equipped with powerful weapons and armor, they are highly resilient and capable of dealing extensive damage with their magic attacks. They are sentient beings, capable of communicating in the common tongue, and are best avoided if possible.[/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]

Whether you're battling a Water Elemental or sneaking past a Cave Claw Crawler, make sure to stay alert and apply tactics! Now, gear up and prepare - Zoria: Age of Shattering launches on March 7, 2024!

notes.title: Passive Stats
notes.content:
In Zoria: Age of Shattering, a classic tactical RPG with fluid turn-based combat, you can protect your characters by investing points in Stamina or giving them appropriate equipment, which will boost their Armor and Magic Armor stats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/1f9e7c8675221ce9d43b96d7adf34cbfa979afbb.png[/img]
Stamina will also influence the characters' Initiative. The higher the Initiative (displayed on-screen), the faster your character will act during an encounter. Pay attention to the queue, as it may help you decide to attack which foe will be the most beneficial for you.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/4e010c5757dff2727441915996a85a2051185731.png[/img]
The higher this stat is, the bigger the chance you'll deal extra damage during the fight. Agility or Intelligence influences Crit Chance – depending on which is your character's dominant (it will be marked in stats, don't worry 😉 ).  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/f9ff436dfbb618e90976fec8c02d418868254366.png[/img]
In Zoria, Hit Chance is influenced by the level difference between the character and the enemy. The higher the level of an enemy compared to the character, the lower the chance to hit it.

notes.title: Major Improvements! 🤩 Monthly Changelog
notes.content:
[h2]Commanders! [/h2]

We're excited to share with you what's changed within this month in Zoria: Age of Shattering. We've implemented some elements you haven't seen before, as well as further improved features already in the game. Let's jump into it! 

[h2]⚔️ Speed Button During Encounter[/h2]
Say goodbye to long, drawn-out battles. With our new speed button, you can now control the pace of your encounters. This feature adds a new level of strategy and enjoyment to our turn-based combat system. Plus, we've added a handy marker on the turn queue, so you'll always know when the turn ends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/4e010c5757dff2727441915996a85a2051185731.png[/img]
[h2]⚔️ Combat Review[/h2]
Knowledge is power, and our new combat review feature gives you plenty of it. After each battle, you'll receive a summary, complete with EXP gained and any additional bonuses. And if you take on a new enemy, your journal will get updated with a new entry, which will be shown on-screen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/e5e22fc466adc86cc10ad190fc8c4a7212c15e3e.png[/img]
[h2]⚔️ Partial Voice Over[/h2]
We implemented a partial voice over that really breathes life into our characters. Now, characters will say the beginning of their dialogue lines, which adds a new layer of depth and personality. Hearing the voices of characters complements the storytelling aspect of Zoria, and makes them more real and dynamic. Soon, we'll show you what the voice overs actually sound like, so stay tuned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/11e3f2a7a926854c14d3200d280454d89a58e0b2.png[/img]
[h2]⚔️ Map Improvements[/h2]
Navigation just got a whole lot easier. We added checkpoints to the map and made it more user-friendly, so you can focus on the adventure at hand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/be33dcff6215f8c0ff0fdae7910e3d4a8cbce136.png[/img]
[h2]⚔️ UI Improvements[/h2]
Finding and managing your equipment now should be a breeze. We touched up the equipment tab for better usability - new items will now be clearly marked, so you'll never miss a new addition to your inventory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/1f9e7c8675221ce9d43b96d7adf34cbfa979afbb.png[/img]
[h2]⚔️ Overall Quality Improvements[/h2]
We worked on the overall quality of graphics in Zoria. From on-screen fonts and effects to the look of characters in and outside of cutscenes - the edges are visibly sharper. We also improved the journal with quests, making it more readable and easier to use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/3b3c72cedbdc875812978321d74d419f9770b307.png[/img]

notes.title: Stats - how to build your hero?
notes.content:
[h2]Commanders![/h2]

In Zoria: Age of Shattering, a classic tactical RPG, you can develop the character as you like. However, maintaining a balance and distributing stat points when leveling up according to the character's class will make the game more enjoyable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/f9ff436dfbb618e90976fec8c02d418868254366.png[/img]
If you'd like to play a warrior-type character in Zoria, it'd be best to invest your points in Strength (if you're planning to be in the first line or carry a shield) or Agility. Agility better suits more nimble heroes or those attacking from a distance).

Casters, on the other hand, will benefit the most from Agility and, of course, Intellect, which will influence their Mana pool and Crit Chance. High Intellect means your character can cast more spells, and they will hit your enemies harder! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/96accf094d6d714ad3ea773ea9865bfa249bacdc.png[/img]
Stamina will increase your character's health. It'll be extremely important, no matter what type of hero you'll be playing as, especially at the beginning of the game! Zoria can be challenging, so there's no point in making it harder, right?

notes.title: How to train a dragon? Asking for a friend.
notes.content:
[h2]Hello, Commander! ⚔️[/h2]

[b]We understand that you are eagerly anticipating the Full Release date.[/b] Before we discuss the updates, we want to address this topic. We promise to announce the release date soon, but we're taking our time to ensure that we deliver a polished product that takes into account all factors that could impact the launch. [b]We appreciate your patience during this process[/b], and we are working hard to make sure that the final product is worth the wait.

Here are the latest updates to excite you for Zoria's upcoming release. 😃 Check out what we've got for you in this [b]Monthly Changelog #9[/b]!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/52515afea417ae9395f583be19c0603aeebd80ba.png[/img]

[h3]QA Testing [/h3]
We are in the final stretch of development before the release of Zoria: Age of Shattering. At this point, we are heavily focused on[b] quality assurance testing[/b] throughout the entire game. This process is essential to optimize the game and eliminate bugs or glitches. In addition, we have spent the past month testing and refining some [b]exciting new features that we have yet to reveal[/b], such as follower management and outpost upgrades. We can't wait for you to try them out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/9e75e344162b1c1dc629dbb1a1de1ffa1582b9c4.png[/img]
[i]A metaphor of us fighting bugs.[/i]

[h3]Content Lock [/h3]
We have finally achieved a significant milestone in game development - [b]the content lock[/b]. This is an important step where we decide that we won't add any more content to the game. This decision allows us to focus solely on refining and polishing the existing content. As you may know, it was not an easy decision because when you are creating something, there is always an inner critic that keeps telling you that you could do it better or differently. Many of you can probably relate to that feeling. 😅

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/70c85c1fb09fd4a745fa053c7119b3d85b54eedb.png[/img]
[i]My inner critic would never say "perfect" 😥[/i]

[h3]Intro Scene [/h3]
Recently, we have been working on creating a story-based introduction scene for the game. The goal is to introduce you to the game effortlessly despite the complicated circumstances you may find yourself in. 😉 [b]We're really pleased with the progress so far, and we hope you will enjoy it too![/b] As a sneak peek, here's a preview of what's in store:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/5bf4f02aadd43f7a78357bdd07cb5b36cd818d10.gif[/img]

[h3]Dragon[/h3]
We added a couple of events during which you will be able to interact with a [b]dragon[/b]. Beware! Despite its rather adorable demeanor, dragons found in the wild can and will hurt you. 🐲

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/bb47b192f6279bc67f85e438db6a226b3c4a4c52.jpg[/img]

[h3]Fun Videos[/h3]
Our publishing team had a lot of fun while creating short and funny videos that were inspired by Zoria. You can easily find them on Anshar Publishing's [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@ansharpublishing]TikTok[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/@AnsharPublishing]YouTube[/url] channels. We believe that you may find them amusing and maybe even inspiring enough to create your own Zoria cosplay! 😃

notes.title: About our Release Date
notes.content:
[h2]Commanders![/h2]
We have some important news about the release of Zoria: Age of Shattering. Over the past few weeks, we've been rigorously QA testing the game to ensure it's ready for release. However, our latest tests indicate that[b] the game will not meet our satisfaction level by October 5th.[/b] Therefore, we must delay the launch by a few weeks. 

We understand that this may be disappointing news, but we believe that taking this extra time to test and refine the game will ultimately result in a better experience for all of us. We appreciate your patience and understanding. Your anticipation and excitement for the game have been a constant source of motivation for us, and we're incredibly grateful for your support.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/8f358daac9e9cb88d2d8e91861f3110dcaf65de6.png[/img]
[h2]Fighting with bugs[/h2]
For the past few weeks, we've been collaborating with an external QA team, who have reported over 280 issues to us. While most of these are minor, our small team of three people, including [b]one programmer handling most of the issues[/b] (poor Gabi), finds this number too significant to be sure that by October 5th, we will be able to deliver a game that we can confidently deem as a finished product.

[b]Therefore, our primary focus for the upcoming days will be intensive QA testing to determine precisely how many more weeks of additional bug fixing we require.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/fd0d1948cb7693809e54dab27d96151ac7e465b4.png[/img]
[h2]Working on balance[/h2]
In addition to bug fixing, we're also working on enhancing the game's balance to provide you with a smooth experience. It involves careful adjustment of character and item stats and giving a second look at all the effects, etc.

Ultimately, thorough testing is the key to delivering a game that meets your expectations and our high standards. We still need a bit more time to finalize the game and accurately determine a new release date. Stay tuned! We are doing our best to make it worth the wait. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/84ef4923c9e37789a0ed25de41382727c2000282.png[/img]
[h2]The new demo[/h2]
[b]We recently launched a new demo, and we strongly encourage you to play it and share your feedback. [/b]A questionnaire will be available after you finish the demo, and we'd love to hear your thoughts.

In the upcoming weeks, our representatives will attend [b]PAX West[/b] in Seattle and [b]WASD[/b] in London. We'll demonstrate the demo and gather last-minute feedback before we wrap up production.

[b]We are dedicated to regularly updating you on our progress.[/b] You can always find us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/k3fPxX8]Discord[/url] or [url=https://twitter.com/ZoriaGame]Twitter/X[/url]. [h1]Hello, Commanders![/h1]

Before we get to the changelog, let's share with you the latest decision we made.

[h2]Important Announcement[/h2]

[b]Due to the congested September release schedule, we chose to delay the release date of Zoria.[/b] Titles such as Baldur's Gate 3, Starfield, and Lies of P, to name just a few, release around the same period. While some of you have pointed it out as we announced our release date, we couldn't put Zoria, an indie game, and other AAA production titles, in the same league (but thanks to those of you who did, we took it as a huge compliment!). Long story short, we feel that shifting our release date would give Zoria the attention and exposure it deserves.

That said, we settled that [b]October 5th[/b] will be the best day to release Zoria: Age of Shattering. It's just a few days later than our initial release date, but we believe this time will provide a space between releases needed for Zoria to shine through. ☀️ Additionally, since every single day at this point will be extremely precious, it will give us extra time to polish the game.

We also [b]enhanced the customization options[/b]. Firstly, we improved support for colors, shader material modifications, and emissive materials. We even added a color picker! Secondly, we added a dynamic [b]size and scale control of the human body[/b]. Thanks to that feature, you'll be able to adjust body proportions and create different shapes of faces, making each character one-of-a-kind.

Furthermore, we implemented a wide array of styling features, such as various[b] hairstyles, faces, makeup options, eyebrows, facial hair[/b], etc., to ensure characters will come in a wide variety. Lastly, we incorporated numerous [b]new item models[/b] that can be used for character design, providing even more customization options.

We developed a useful tool for creating icons for in-game items. We're using it to create icons for all weapons and armor pieces in the inventory. We plan on using it to create portraits for heroes made with Character Creator as well, but we're still working on that 😉

Besides that, we're reworking and adjusting the [b]outposts [/b]to improve clarity and make them more intuitive. notes.title: Changing plans
notes.content:
[h1]Adventurers! ⚔️ [/h1]

After careful consideration, we came to the conclusion that Zoria doesn't need Early Access, because we're ready to [b]make a Full Release this September. [/b]

Let's fill you in on which arguments helped us make this decision. 


[h2]Content Evaluation [/h2]

We've been working on Zoria tirelessly for some time now. There are surely creators among you that know the feeling (or rather a need) of polishing your project until you think it's perfect. The truth is, the inner critic might never tell you you got there 😉 

We evaluated our latest milestone and realized that [b]Zoria is so close to being completed that putting it on Early Access would only water down our progress[/b]. Launching Zoria in EA would mean launching an incomplete game for a few months when in reality, [b]we only need a few months to finish the game. [/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/93b2744ee1ed307e222291c099b6dc51acc2e8b5.png[/img]
[i]Can be treated as a metaphor for us being close to finishing the game. Also, a nice screenshot.[/i]

[h2]Zoria is not that type of game [/h2]

Early Access has its benefits, don't get us wrong - that's why we considered it in the first place. Zoria has been in development for some time now, and we were eager to finally show it to you. But games that benefit from EA are hugely the ones that provide [b]service[/b]. From the very beginning, [b]we designed Zoria to be a complete, single-player adventure. [/b]We want you to be able to fully immerse yourself in the fantasy world of Zoria without the need to turn a blind eye to unpolished elements.  

And finally, the argument that appealed to us the most. 


[h2]Delivering Full Release sooner [/h2]

By launching Zoria in Early Access, we'd need to change our focus from finishing the game to hotfixing and bugfixing. Instead, we can stay on track and instead [b]release the game sooner[/b]. In fact, we made an honest calculation and decided that [b][u]Zoria: Age of Shattering will launch on September 19th, 2023.[/u]  [/b]

We got excited to get your reactions and feedback to Zoria ASAP, as it'd be an[b] invaluable source of information and a boost of encouragement.[/b] But you can still do that by following us on Twitter and Facebook or joining our Discord server ⚔️ At the end of the day, we're working with playtesters as well as with members of our wonderful community (thank you!) to make [b]the most magical experience possible. We are slowly getting to the point where we're polishing the game and getting it ready for you to play 🤫 This month we were not only ticking off things from our "to-do list" but also working closely with [b]playtesters [/b]and polishing the game based on their [b]reactions [/b]and [b]feedback[/b].   

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/0a407404f9d5762f805bd3061ee430b68ec65e67.jpg[/img]  

Anyway, what's changed outside of typical [b]bug fixing[/b], [b]UI adjusting[/b], and [b]polishing [/b]already implemented features?  

[h2]Upgraded party's downtime  [/h2]

We want the resting mechanic to play an important role in Zoria's gameplay. On the one hand, because of the [b]strategic point of view[/b] and how it benefits the party. The player can organize camps to [b]heal wounded followers[/b] or [b]exchange them for new ones[/b]. On the other hand, because of the [b]bonds the player can establish[/b] with various characters.   

Since Zoria is a roleplaying game, we implemented a dialogue system during the rest, enabling the player to [b]learn more about the followers they're traveling with[/b], get to know them better, and decide who they like best.  

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/4ded41b97749d04907cef7d2b93446f58ef5345c.png[/img]

Moreover, we designed some quests that can be triggered by setting up the camp, so [b]beware[/b]! It could be wildlife or bandits attacking or a follower coming up to you and saying, "we need to talk." It's hard to say which one is worse 😬  

[h2]A more dynamic camera during dialogue  [/h2]

Some quest dialogue would benefit from more dynamic camera action. We [b]improved close-ups[/b] to make it look and feel better 😜   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/fcc86497c5493069241ae64e206919e926847cde.png[/img]

[h2]Follower's status changes when they're not an active member of the party  [/h2]

The game treats the follower as an NPC unless they get recruited to the party. The player can interact with NPC followers and see them roaming in the world when they're [b]out of duty[/b]. Additionally, followers' models will [b]respond in real-time[/b] to the player changing their [b]gear [/b]and [b]weapons[/b].   

[h2]New equipment  [/h2]

Speaking of which, we got our characters some [b]new armor and equipment[/b] designs! We're integrating them with the character creator to give players more options to customize their hero. We're still planning on adding even more armor in the future, not only for fashion's sake 😉   

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/8213cde3c5c5d96a2bec6f97db5188559ea14b27.png[/img]

There is some exciting news coming soon 😉 Stay tuned!

notes.content:
[h1]Hello, Commander![/h1]

Working on Zoria: Age of Shattering is an [b]exciting[/b] but also [b]challenging[/b] experience. The ideas are endless, and expectations - yours and ours - are high. This month we introduced many valuable changes to the game. Are you ready? Welcome to [b]Monthly Changelog #2[/b]! ːsteamhappyː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/317b055d31d32918383f57710c9d3fcd342e7cd5.png[/img]
[i]A party ready to explore each corner. Do I smell... chest?![/i]

[h2]Remodeled and expanded locations[/h2]

Rithvale had a complete makeover. We needed to rebuild it to match it with our current level of quality. Rithvale will become your homebase and your safe haven you'll long for after a long journey. 

Players will now have quests available (both sidequests and main quests), making it a more[b] lively area worth revisiting at different stages of the game. [/b]

Do you remember Shrieking Pass? Some of you might have seen it in the demo from 2 years ago. We felt this location could be more interesting, so we decided to revisit it, with some new places and adventures ːsteamhappyː Now it is not only an area where the story takes place but also a part of the story on its own.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/49dbdd63e06bb600173d0916c5c6d527ef4be3a2.png[/img]
[i]This is totally how we rebuilt our locations. We evacuate everyone, and then we lure a dragon and four Trolls to raze the city to the ground. Easy-peasy.[/i]

[h2]Attacks of Opportunity[/h2]

RPG players are most likely familiar with this system. Certain characters will be able to strike an enemy unit in combat as it moves next to them. It can be a very [b]satisfying[/b] move that'll prevent your opponents from running away from you and has a significant chance to finish them off without the need to chase them around the map (and possibly get into a trap).

Character Creator was a Strech Goal on Kickstarter that we unfortunatelly didn't reached [b]BUT[/b] we decided to add it after all. ːsteammockingː We believe that creating your own character in an RPG adds a lot of value to a roleplaying aspect of the game. notes.title: Dev Diary #8 - Characters, classes and team composition
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome, travelers of the Uram continent! [/h2]

I have gathered you here today to tell you about your upcoming duties and the companions with whom you will [b]undertake them. [/b]The times are hard, and the quest is challenging, so you must be extremely cautious when selecting [b]who you will befriend. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/b4bb1e1cb8f902e28f0f2142ee67e24ed6283b97.png[/img]

In Zoria,[b] ten different specializations[/b] of warriors may join our team. You, as a commander, will be out of this category, serving more as a [b]support but in a unique way[/b]. Two characters will represent each class with their [b]own story, motivations, and wits. [/b]

Your followers are critical to the success of your mission. Whether recruited through the Inn or from various quests, your companions represent your [b]most significant investment and resource[/b] since your adventure is squad-based, and only good use of the squad system can ensure success.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/BtVnXc3/r4.png[/img]

For most of the exploration, you will [b]control the main character in real time[/b], with the squad following every step you take. However, during the combat, every character will be[b] ready to carry out your order.[/b]

Let's have a closer look at some of the classes in Zoria. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/4a0178d27ed54a2ccbda304efa855cea208a154d.png[/img]

In addition to the above, the game will also include the following:
[list]
[b][*]Ranger
[*]Thief
[*]Wizard
[*]Priest
[*]Bard
[*]Nightwarden[/b]
[/list]
[h2]Team composition[/h2]
As you've probably already guessed, [b]only a good combination[/b] of your companions' classes can bring success on the battlefield. A team of rangers alone would be spectacular and look great on defensive walls, while their effectiveness would be [b]very low in a close encounter. [/b]

[img]https://i.ibb.co/JQ6Nc51/ezgif-com-gif-maker.gif[/img]

There is another reason why you should be especially careful in choosing teammates. In the world of Zoria, there are objects that only a [b]character with the right abilities can interact with[/b]. Hence, [b]Battle Clerics can interact with Shrines of Nerdalye [/b]to replenish the party's health, and Wizard can [b]create magical bridges[/b] over which the whole team can safely cross to the other side.  

------------------

Concluding my story, I hope it has made you look forward to Zoria even more.[b] The year 2023 is very close[/b], and in a few months, you will see the result of our dream to create a full-blooded RPG. In the meantime, we wish you a [b]peaceful holiday and a happy new year! 
[/b]

notes.title: What's new in the world of Zoria? Monthly changelog.
notes.content:
Hello commanders! 

It has been approximately six weeks since our Kickstarter campaign, and throughout this period, we have been tirelessly working to bring you a game that guarantees a remarkable experience. Today, we are excited to present a sneak peek of our current development progress through a collection of fresh screenshots. We sincerely hope you enjoy them and that they heighten your anticipation for what's to come!

However, before we delve into the main content, we kindly request your support by voting for Zoria in the IndieDB's Indie of the Year poll. With a vast community like yours, we firmly believe that we can secure a prominent position in this competition dedicated to indie game enthusiasts.

[url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/zoria-age-of-shattering][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/070d9a93bf60633e767eed8a809110243b4bbfd7.jpg[/img][/url]

You can cast a vote on our IndieDB page [url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/zoria-age-of-shattering]>>here<< [/url]

[b]Now, let's move on with the changelog.[/b]

[b][h3]Nightwarden Class[/h3][/b]
As some of you may recall, one of the secret goals of the Kickstarter campaign was reaching 50%, and it unlocked a new class - [b]fearless and violent Nightwarden[/b]. First, we had some rough ideas on how this class should act on the battlefield, and during the last month, we managed to finish the profile of this class.

Nightwardens [b]will use fire [/b]on the battlefield because this is the most effective deterring of monsters. Having Nightwarden in your team will significantly increase the group morale, as [b]Nightwardens fear no death[/b] and can teach their teammates how to act the same. On top of that, Nightwardens know that the night is short; therefore, [b]they must act quickly. [/b]

[img]https://i.ibb.co/Tbwhbsn/Sequence-01.gif[/img]

[b][h3]Day-night cycle[/h3][/b]
Well, what would be the point of the existence of Nightwardens if there were no night, wasn't it? That's why we've been spending the last few weeks polishing the day and night cycle in the world of Zoria, which will not only limit the amount of sunlight but also [b]affect certain events and behaviors at specific times of the day.[/b] 

And remember, the world of Zoria is not a safe enough place during the day. I dread to think how it will be at night. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/93915a48baa4f2479e17f23caf1e3c518aa83b44.png[/img]

[b][h3]Lake Mannor[/h3][/b]
A castle in the middle of rocky mountains, a fisherman's hut, fog hovering over the lake, and rumors of a secret lurking beneath the surface of this reservoir. [b]Don't forget to chat with a hunter [/b]who stays in the area, as he will have something to say about the place. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/be8af7db7561bac19c67085c8531cdf6aea06404.png[/img]

[b][h3]New enemy - Troll[/h3][/b]
What is it - it has two legs, pointy ears, smells horrible, and you wouldn't entrust your pet to its care? No, it's not a green-clad boy rescuing a princess. [b]It's a nasty troll lurking for fresh meat, [/b]inattentively straying near his lair. Just look at this monstrosity. It's probably time to show him that treating poor animals like this doesn't seem right. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/d82af1487ef059090674bc53069b9c4c76b038c5.png[/img]

That's all for today, and we're back to making the game. Let us know what you think of the above features, and don't forget to join our Discord - it's a smug place for RPG & coffee lovers (but if you are more of a tea person, you are more than welcome too.) 

[url=https://discord.com/invite/k3fPxX8][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/329fdb66137bcd2c299ca4d231619a03b531062d.png[/img][/url]


Stay tuned,
Zoria Team

notes.title: Dev Diary #6 - Religion
notes.content:
[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ansharpublishing/zoria-age-of-shattering][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/34298a2a31aa42ec44dd612837a81cbd9a1669f6.jpg[/img][/url]

Hey everyone!

[h3]Zoria lore is huge! Today we want to focus on the topic of religion, which, of course, is present in the game's world.[/h3]

We believe it will be interesting to talk more about this; religion is important to us as people, therefore why not dig into this a little bit? There are three main churches:
 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/393575351fb4f653c731ce316cff27f028c4b9f7.jpg[/img]

 
[h1]1. The Church of Torath, also known as The Church Zoria’s Light[/h1]

Generally, Monotheistic, with smaller figures involved in the mythos, established religion within Elion and extended with varying influence into most of the Uram continent.

[b]Gods[/b]:

- [b]Torath [/b]- God of Light, believed to carry the sun on his back across the sky and responsible for bringing light, heat, and general well-being to the citizen of Zoria.

- [b]Torhuz[/b] – God-like figure, brother of Torath and polar opposite. Believed to dwell in the depths of the night and fight an eternal battle with Torath for control of the skies.

With the dual-moon specific of Zoria, two eclipses are happening, one incomplete and one that completely covers the sun, believed to be instances of a great war between the two brothers and bad omens for the people.
 The stars are believed to be spirits sent by Torath to light the night sky and prevent Torhuz from bringing eternal darkness to the world.
 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/a74f4fed9dae3b756176997126b3c3a88d983d7d.jpg[/img]

 
[h1]2. The Church of the 9 Gods[/h1]

Polytheistic, widespread throughout the Uram continent. Based on ancient humanoid gods said to inhabit Vrukmanar, the volcanic landmass east of Uram.

[b]Gods[/b]:

[b]Athys [/b]- Goddess of Light, governor and chief of all gods (patron saint of Priests and Battle Clerics)

[b]Dhases [/b]- God of Prosperity (patron saint of Bards, Merchants, and Traders)

[b]Garom[/b]- God of War and Fire(patron saint of Mercenaries Battle Clerics and Lancers)

[b]Amaldir[/b] - God of Earth and Nature, Husband of Mei-Devi(patron saint of Rangers, Farmers, Commoners, and Hunters)

notes.title: Dev Diary #5 – Combat in Zoria
notes.content:
[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ansharpublishing/zoria-age-of-shattering][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/34298a2a31aa42ec44dd612837a81cbd9a1669f6.jpg[/img][/url]

[b]Hello commanders![/b]

In today's Dev Diary, we'll cover what many tactical RPG fans like best: [b]combat[/b]. We designed it to be dynamic, fluid, and inviting to engage. But how did we achieve that? Enjoy the read below!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/27b347415b632a8ddfef6af94b31a65707dbeb07.jpg[/img]

[h1]Classes[/h1]

In your team, you will have characters of different classes, each of which will have a [b]tree of 16 skills[/b], from which you will choose 9, giving you the chance to [b]try other builds and tactics[/b]. For example, the Wizard class can pick all the water-based spells, fire-based spells, or a mix of them. The same Wizard class can follow the route of [b]AoE or single target damage or favor a more protection-oriented build[/b].

Abilities vary from [b]single target to effect over time and area of effect[/b]. Some include [b]summoning, spawning area-of-effect items on the battlefield, or using line-of-sight and blocking enemies' paths.[/b]

Your protagonist, the Commander, Andar Witherell, is a special class on its own and can either go the route of [b]damage dealer, shield buffer, or healer, with a lot of flexibility in its skills[/b].

When completing a team, the critical thing to pay attention to is [b]class synergy[/b]. Classes can protect, heal, or empower other characters, and creative use of special abilities (taunts and control) can provide [b]exciting encounters[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/b6350ef01fa51013dd93247e80ffd9cea592f911.jpg[/img]

[h1]Resources[/h1]

There are several combat-specific resources: Action Points, Focus, and Mana/Energy.

[b]Action Points[/b]: Each character or enemy character has two Action Points. You can use these points for moving (both APs), moving and abilities use (1AP + 1AP), or if in a favorable position, abilities only (2APs). Remember that some high-impact abilities cost more than others and have a 2AP cost.

[b]Focus[/b]: Each class generates Focus by using other abilities or by the use of a potion. Focus is always 0 at the beginning of combat and can reach a maximum of 100.

[b]Mana/Energy[/b]: This set of resources is directly connected to the Intellect and Agility stats and can be replenished by resting or using potions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/a56c398b9e41ba6d919c54e0aaf0c38978c4af32.jpg[/img]

[h1]Battlefield[/h1]

Zoria is[b] not using a traditional grid-based system[/b], thus making the combat a bit more fluid. You will still have battlefield obstacles that can hinder you or your enemy.

When observing the environment during the battle, you need to pay attention to [b]using line-of-sight[/b] - your character cannot fire while another party member or enemy is in front of him. The same is true for the enemies - they will move into position to attack a character if they are out of sight. Also, initiating combat near an [b]environment trap[/b] can lead to the creative use of such traps to aid in battle.

But, even if the scales of victory start tipping to you, you can't be sure of your success. The combat is turn-based, but [b]the world around continues to work on the real-time system[/b]. Enemies patrolling nearby can join the action if they get within range, so it can turn simple situations into really complicated fights, depending on the area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/8de9dba5c16ca87f0a0be357a36f6b570d73afed.png[/img]

After this description, we hope you fancy a little skirmish. That's why we invite you to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1159090/zoria_age_of_shattering/]test our free demo[/url] and share any feedback you have.

Until the next one!

notes.title: Dev Diary #2 - Let's talk about the Stats!
notes.content:
Hello adventurers!👋

Today we want to talk about some [b]stats, armor, and attack types[/b] in Zoria. There are a lot of mechanics in the game that we believe we should cover, so you get the idea of what to expect when you jump into the world of Zoria. It's going to be a pretty long diary today, so grab your favorite beverage, snacks and enjoy the guide!

[b]Main Stats[/b]
These stats directly influence the character’s various attributes (health, damage) and the power of a character’s abilities.

 [list]
[*][i]Stamina:[/i] directly affects the character’s health. Especially important early game and the single greatest contributor to player survivability. 
[/list]
 [list]
[*][i]Strength:[/i] especially important for melee characters, directly affects Melee Attack Power and increases the Energy pool for Lancer class and Captain. It also increases block power for characters wearing a Shield.
[/list]
 [list]
[*][i]Agility:[/i] increases Ranged Attack Power for Ranger. Increases Melee Attack Power for Thief. Increases Melee Attack Power for Lancer, Kingsman, Battle Cleric, and Captain to a smaller degree. Increases Energy pool for Ranger, Thief, and Kingsman. Increases Crit Chance with values depending on the class. Increases Armor.
[/list]
 [list]
[*][i]Intellect:[/i] Increases Spell Power. Increases Magic Armor. Increases Crit Chance for magic abilities. Increases Mana pool for Wizard, Necromancer, Priest, Battle Cleric, Bard.
[/list]
 [list]
[*][i]Armor:[/i] reduces the amount of damage received from physical abilities and effects.
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Magic Armor:[/i] reduces the amount of damage received from magic abilities and effects.
[/list] 
 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/d352c0405c47997bd4541b02bc72e2d49892bb94.png[/img]

 
[b]Secondary Stats:[/b]
 [list]
[*][i]Initiative:[/i] it influences the character’s place in the combat queue at the start and where it will be placed in the queue once that character’s turn is finished. A character with a high Initiative value will be placed higher in the combat queue once its turn is completed than a character with a low Initiative value.
[/list]
 [list]
[*][i]Hit Chance:[/i] chance to hit with an ability. It is directly influenced by the level difference between the character and the enemy. The higher the level of an enemy compared to the character, the lower the Hit Chance.
[/list]
 [list]
[*][i]Crit Chance:[/i] Critical chance is influenced by the dominant stat for that class – Agility or Intellect.
[/list]

 
[b]Elemental Resistances:[/b]
All magic effects belong to a type of elemental magic.
 [list]
[*][i]Fire Magic[/i]
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Water Magic[/i]
[/list] 
 [list]
[*][i]Nature Magic[/i]
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Arcane Magic[/i]
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Death Magic[/i]
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Light Magic[/i]
[/list]
 
Light and Death Magic are in direct opposition, with Death Magic wielders being especially weak to Light Magic and Light Magic wielders especially weak to Death Magic abilities.
Enemies weak to Fire Magic are equally weak to physical Fire effects, like the Fire Arrow Ranger ability.
Elemental resistances mitigate a percent of the incoming damage from that specific element. Gear pieces with elemental resistance have values representing their elemental resistance. Depending on the level, these values translate to different percentages of elemental resistance, making a low-level gear piece more effective in elemental protection for the appropriate level character.

[b]Effects:[/b]
These effects are placed on the character by various abilities and can be temporary (only during combat) or permanent (must be removed by resting, using a potion, or in the Outpost). Each effect influences the player’s stats differently:

 [list]
[*][i]Sunder:[/i] can be applied by physical abilities. Decreases the player Armor and can stack multiple effects.
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Wound:[/i] can be applied by physical abilities. Decreases the player Initiative while active.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Bleed:[/i] can be applied by physical abilities. Deals damage over time to the character until removed.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Stun:[/i] can be applied by any kind of ability. Locks the character in the current position in the combat queue for its duration.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Poison:[/i] can be applied by Nature abilities. Decreases Hit Chance.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Disease:[/i] can be applied by Nature abilities. DecreasesAgilityandIntellect.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Curse:[/i] can be applied by Death abilities. Decreases Strength and Magic Armor.
[/list] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/2f17367010ffd68b9e27e134a8e94fe65c84552c.png[/img]

These effects do not show on the Character Stat sheet but in the abilities description for each ability that places a certain effect. Some enemies can be immune to certain types of effects, making the abilities that place those effects less effective. This immunity will be shown in the Compendium entry for each enemy.

[b]Stats influence on abilities:[/b]
The power of each ability of a certain class is affected by the main stat. Because of this, different builds for a class can benefit from a different main stat.
 
As an example, below are some of the Kingsman’s abilities and the stats affecting their power:

[list]
[*][i]Strength:[/i] Basic Attack, Vanquish thy Foe, Avenger Strike, Bash of Wrath.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Agility:[/i] Shield Wall, King's Resolve, Deflect, Hold the Line, Avatar of Protection.
[/list] 
[list]
[*][i]Intellect[/i]: Magic Absorption, King's Fire.
[/list]
 
[i]Fatigue:[/i] is a special stat central to the Fatigue and Outpost recovery mechanic. We will introduce more details on this mechanic in a dedicated post later.
 
Together with the Stats update, we are also introducing new stats to armor and weapons.

[list]
[*]Durability: all weapons and armor now have certain durability that decreases with each combat. Once a gear item’s durability reaches 0, that item is no longer usable and does not contribute to the character’s stats.
[/list]

[b]Armor Types:[/b]
[list]
[*][i]Light Armor[/i]: worn by Wizard, Necromancer, and Priest classes.
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Medium Armor:[/i] worn by Ranger, Thief, Bard classes, and the Captain.
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Hardened Armor:[/i] worn by the Ranger, Kingsman, Lancer, Battle Cleric classes, and the Captain.
[/list]
[list]
[*][i]Heavy Armor:[/i] worn by the Kingsman and Lancer classes.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/c625f158f8acd6fcbda6978ec466ee9f3b103fb7.png[/img]
 
[b]Weapon Damage and Spell Damage:[/b]
[list]
[*]All weapons now have a weapon damage stat. This damage is added to the base attack of the character using that weapon.
[/list]
[list]
[*]Specific caster weapons, like the staff, have a Spell Damage stat instead of Weapon Damage.
[/list]

Stay tuned for future updates, as there is much more we want to present to you!

Cheers,
Team Zoria

notes.title: Dev Diary - Let's introduce ourselves!
notes.content:
[h3]Hey everyone! 👋


We are super excited about the [b]Kickstarter [/b]campaign, and we want to thank every single one of you who decided and will decide to support [i][b]Zoria: Age of Shattering[/b][/i]! [/h3]

Many of you may not know the story behind the [b]Tiny Trinket Games[/b]. We think that for the first [b]Dev Diary[/b], it will be perfect to introduce ourselves and give you a little backstory on our first steps in the gaming industry. 

Ladies and gentlemen, meet our team! 

[b]Stefan Nicolescu (Fane) [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/95325276ebb62fb5679827413078c680595f0965.jpg[/img]

[i]I have worked in the gaming industry since 2004, in several roles, from [b]QA tester[/b] to [b]QA Manager[/b], to PM, Level Designer, and [b]Game Designer[/b]. I have been working on mobile games in my spare time, but my mind was always set on a [b]full-fledged PC RPG game[/b]. As time passed, [b]my dream came true[/b], and now I am in charge of all [b]creative aspects[/b] for [b]Zoria AoS[/b] - from mechanics to level design and environment design, UI, SFX, and animations. I love games, but most of all, I love making them. Nowadays, I enjoy the day-to-day process, as I am doing the thing that defines me. [/i]

[b]Stefan Nitescu (Neles)  [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/23a7d45da3b436df882219cec58b0191d68eed35.jpg[/img]

[i]Passionate about games since childhood, especially [b]RPGs [/b]and [b]story-driven games[/b], my background is not what you would call a classic game developer background, with studies in [b]architecture [/b]and [b]business[/b].  

Working on a game like Zoria was something I always wanted to do - to participate in the creation of a big, detailed, magical world that you can lose yourself into.  

Apart from the day-to-day administrative activities of [b]Tiny Trinket Games[/b], I'm in charge of the implementation of quests, actions, interactions, triggers, in short, [b]Quests[/b], [b]Events[/b], and [b]Dialogues (QED)[/b]. Together with Fane, [b]I have written the lore[/b] of the world of [b]Zoria [/b]and created the story's overall [b]narrative structure[/b], a part of the quests you will be playing throughout the game.  

I hope you will have as much fun playing [b]Zoria: Age of Shattering[/b] as we had creating/working on it. [/i]

[b]Gabriel Ivanica (Gabi) [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/82b7a0341b1157071d498affec2910afe51290cc.jpg[/img]

[i]I've always been fond of video games and computers, but the road from playing them to making them was long. While studying, I discovered my passion for [b]graphics programming[/b] and [b]game engines[/b] since they are the perfect combination between complex technical sciences and the visual output of my work. I’m a software engineer with a [b]master’s degree[/b] in [b]Advanced Techniques for Computer Graphics[/b]. I worked on various University Research Projects to expand my knowledge of real-time graphics computing and general application software architecture. I also love sharing the things I learn, so I started teaching computer graphics and game programming at university or in the game industry in collaboration with [b]Ubisoft Bucharest Studio[/b].  

Working on Zoria has been the part that I enjoyed the most in the last [b]five years[/b]. My dream is not only to launch this game but to continue to work on feature versions and [b]expand the realm of possibilities[/b] of what gamers can do in Zoria through new features, mechanics, and visual feedback. What motivates me is the opportunity to work on a personal project that I love and grow it into something that others may experience and find enjoyable. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/fc526700b9044d4cc1b33de94d574319d3ee44a9.png[/img]

[b]Tiny Trinket Games[/b] took its current form in 2017, and our purpose was to develop games for PC. The first game under the name Tiny Trinket Games, [b][i]Azuran Tales: Trials[/i][/b], was launched for PC in 2018, about the same time we started working on the concept that would later become [b][i]Zoria: Age of Shattering[/i][/b]. In 2019 we managed to port [i][b]Azuran Tales[/b][/i] to the Nintendo Switch and have been working on [i][b]Zoria [/b][/i]since. We launched the [i][b]Prologue [/b][/i]in 2020 and the updated Demo in 2021, iterating and improving the systems and the game's overall quality. 

One downside of working on a large game as a small indie team is the time involved in taking the game to where we wanted it, especially since we had to support ourselves in the meantime and could often only work on it in [b]our spare time[/b]. 

[h3][b]Origin story and how we started project Zoria. [/b][/h3]

We (Fane and Neles) have been friends for years, and we've spent lots of hours playing together at [b]Lan parties[/b] back in the day.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/270d91c0f4205f564c741a312b87073fb1cab404.jpg[/img]

Years ago, we’ve been talking about [b]making games[/b] and were both very excited about the idea. One thing led to another, and we decided to try to [b]make it work[/b]. After many prototypes and a long search for a third partner to complete our team, we met Gabi at a gathering at [b]TechHub Bucharest[/b]. 

We set up a meeting, we met, Fane (Stefan Nicolescu) showcased what he did in Unity, and Gabi liked what he saw. From there, it is history, and we are here, now, all three of us, after many, many, many sleepless nights, iterations, meetings, calls, and lots of coffee and green tea (for Gabi). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/ba8e980711ca822cc31ab7652e7aefee034ee8f3.jpg[/img]

The idea for [i][b]Zoria [/b][/i]evolved, and Fane’s and Gabi's skills progressed. Originally the game was supposed to be a [b]Mobile game[/b], but Fane wanted something a bit more and later discovered that the rest of the guys also did. One thing led to another, and [b]from 2D mobile[/b], we moved to [b]2D + 3D characters[/b] and [i][b]Heroes 3[/b][/i] style combat to the free-roaming combat we now have in [i][b]Zoria[/b][/i]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/bc887d7344922e107613f73ca60278e6b8156bdd.jpg[/img]

We started in March or April 2017 when we presented Gabi with the mobile game design document. Many years and a lot of free time spent on nothing else but this. For Stefan Nicolescu, it was a [b]learning curve[/b] in terms of level and environment design; with each iteration each year, the levels would [b]improve[/b]. It took him around three years and thousands of hours to reach consistent levels. The same goes for Gabi to understand more the mechanics Fane needed and for Neles (Stefan Nitescu) as well for understanding and requesting features in the [b]Quest Editor[/b]. Gabi and Neles did an excellent job with the Quest Editor, something that was built from scratch to fit our needs. It is still being upgraded as we discover we need it for a thing not tough possible. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/be86a24241beb519e3314f8f70a3ce0c45032a5a.jpg[/img]

[b][h3]WHAT WAS THE BIGGEST CHALLANGE FOR US? [/h3][/b]

Keeping the team together for so long without seeing a financial gain, fueled only by grit and hope. Then came things like: as the [b]design expanded[/b] - keeping track of all the mechanics, skills, triggers, and progress for creating a quest or a new enemy. There is a lot of information overload at some point. Another challenge for us is trying to keep things small; we are kinda failing at this as the [b]Demos we released so far are like small games in terms of gameplay hours. [/b]

The game changed a lot- an [b]unrecognizable [/b]- [b]from 2D mobile game to a 3D party-based, free-roaming, open-world CRPG.[/b] 

[b][h3]WHAT IS THE BEST FOR YOU ABOUT ZORIA, WHAT ARE YOU MOST PROUD OF? [/h3][/b]

[b]Subjectively [/b]here: it's made by three guys in a [b]"living room,"[/b] as we don't have basements. We're also proud that we landed a good balance between too easy ([i][b]Heroes 3[/b][/i]) and too complex ([i][b]Divinity: Original Sin[/b][/i] combinations), so you can [b]easily get into the game[/b]. 


That sums up our story; there is nothing more to say. We’re a group of friends with the privilege to do what they love! 


Cheers,  

Tiny Trinket Games Team

[url=http://bit.ly/ZoriaKickstarter][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/34298a2a31aa42ec44dd612837a81cbd9a1669f6.jpg[/img][/url]

notes.title: We're Tiny Trinket Games, pleased to meet ya! | Info about free demo
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/edda942b41384476da03e19d248f59f513cc4fad.jpg[/img]

It’s happening!  
 
Hello! Many of you are hearing about us for the first time. Let us quickly introduce ourselves. We're [b]Tiny Trinket Games,[/b] a team of 3 passionate devs from Bucharest, Romania, who dream of creating impactful RPG games. Sounds cliche, right?   

[previewyoutube=a1WlTf7dIvM;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/66f2dbdeed7922965a38219bbea59f5bc8bbdea8.jpg[/img]
  
We've been working on [b]Zoria: Age Shattering[/b] since 2018. We can proudly say we have around 80% of the finished content. We teamed up with [b]Anshar Publishing[/b] to give you guys as many opportunities as possible to get familiar with Zoria. That's why we treat Kickstarter as a part of the community-driven approach to our fans. The collected budget will be spent on improvements and additional content we have ideas for, like new classes, locations, and mechanics, which will make the world of Zoria more complex and offer what players expect from immersive RPGs. We hope you will join us on this journey!   

[url=https://bit.ly/ZoriaKickstarter][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/34298a2a31aa42ec44dd612837a81cbd9a1669f6.jpg[/img][/url]

In the next update, we will unveil more information about Zoria's Lore, and we'll break through every game mechanic. Today we have to stick with the most crucial thing – [b]Zoria: Age of Shattering demo is now available on Steam for free!   [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/6c2dcc4410d40b646f07c51dcbd12ce4b1e66632.jpg[/img]

The demo we're presenting covers a part of the game, which will be available later in the full release. In this build, we wanted to focus on a cross-sectional presentation of the mechanics and story of the Zoria world. To fully enjoy the gameplay, it is essential to remember that each teammate has a skill tree, which requires the distribution of skill points.   

You should also regularly look around by rotating the camera during combat and exploration. Make sure the place you've visited has been viewed from all angles and you haven't missed anything. Have fun with the game: play with the team's configuration, attacks, skills, and development paths. Depending on the skills of your team members, some quests will be able to be completed differently, and some ways and objects will become accessible to you.  


Due to this build's "work-in-progress" nature, you may encounter some minor (hopefully not major!) issues. If this happens, we would appreciate it if you would alert us of them. [b]Please share any feedback with us via the Discord server! [/b]
 

[h2]CONTROLS[/h2]

In-World Shortcuts

[list]
[*] Use your mouse to move. Click on the target you wish your party to move to. 
[*] Hold the right mouse button and drag the mouse to rotate the camera. 
[*] Use the mouse scroll to zoom in and out of the view.

notes.title: Devlog: Crafting
notes.content:
Greetings adventurers of Zoria,

Today is the turn of the Crafting System to receive a thorough presentation. The crafting system is part of the Outpost base and follower management System, but since it is almost complete and ready to go into closed beta testing, we decided to introduce it before the overall presentation of the Outpost.
Crafting in Zoria: Age of Shattering revolves around 2 key elements – recipes and player’s freedom to experiment and optimize.

[b]The Crafting Screen:[/b]
[list]
[*] The screen is split in 3 parts:
[*] Available recipes on the left side
[*] Inventory with all the available materials and crafting items on the right side
[*] The crafting area in the center.
[/list]

Once a recipe is selected, that item’s characteristics, bases stats and requirements appear in the crafting area. Each requirement slot must be filled with the specified number of materials (e.g. 2 crystal slots, 1 metal slots).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/5f09bec8342f81acac27dfda2d06ae4554e81e1e.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] The item’s stats change according to the materials used to fill the slots, the complete stats being visible in the upper part of the central screen.
[*] The lower part of the central screen is where the special slots are located: the Crafting Kit slot and the Unstable Slot.
[*] Below them there is the item’s cost to craft and the Crafting Chance, that will remain 100% as long as no material is added to the Unstable Slot.
[/list]


[b]Recipes:[/b]
In order to craft any item, Armor, Weapon or Trinket, a recipe is necessary. These recipes can be acquired in a number of ways:
[list]
[*] Exploration – either on the main area map or exploring dungeons and hidden places.
[*] Quest rewards – by performing certain tasks and doing various quests.
[*] Missions – by sending characters on unattended missions that reward recipes.
[/list]

Recipes, just like the items they help craft, are grouped by rarity:
[list]
[*] Common
[*] Uncommon
[*] Rare
[*] Exotic
[*] Epic
[/list]

Each recipe allows the player to craft a certain item: Armor, Weapon or Trinket, of the recipe’s rarity.

All recipes have the following:
[list]
[*] Item Level.
[*] Item Type: Armor, Weapon, Trinket
[*] Base Stats – 1 to 3 base stats, specific to the recipe, depending on item rarity.
[*] Item Durability.
[*] Crafting Kit slot. 
[*] Crafting slots, number depending on rarity.
[*] Unstable Slot.
[/list]

[b]Item Level:[/b]
[list]
[*]Each recipe can craft an item of a certain level, its base stats depending on this level as much as the recipe’s rarity.
[/list] 

[b]Item Type:[/b]
[list]
[*] For Armors – Armor Type – light, medium, hardened, heavy
[*] For Weapons – Weapon Type – sword, axe, dagger, …
[/list]

[b]Base stats, depending on item types:[/b]
[list]
[*] Armors can have 1-3 Main Stats, depending on rarity - Stamina, Strength, Agility, Intellect.
[*] Weapons can have 1-3 Main or Secondary Stats, depending on rarity. 
[*] Shields can have 1-3 Main Stats, depending on rarity and also have a Block Chance Stat.
[*] Trinkets can have 1-3 Secondary Stats, depending on rarity.
[/list]

These stats are fixed for each recipe and will add their values to the custom slots of the recipe.

[b]Item Durability:[/b]
[list]
[*] All items have a base durability. This base durability is based on the Common Crafting Kit.
[*] The items durability can be improved by using better Crafting Kits.
[/list]

[b]Crafting Kit Slot[/b]
[list] 
[*] Crafting Kits are the base of any item to be crafted. 
[*] The Common Crafting Kit can be used to craft any item, either weapon or armor, and it comes with a base Durability value. 
[*] Other Crafting Kits can be used to craft specific items of 	greater durability – Uncommon, Rare and Exotic Crafting Kits provide greater durability for the crafted item, but they are specific to an item type.
[*] The type of Crafting Kit used is entirely at the player’s discretion, there are no limitations within the recipes.
[/list]

[b]Freedom to experiment and optimize:[/b]

The Crafting Slots and Unstable Slot together allow the player to experiment and craft a number of different items based on the same recipe, depending on the materials used. 

[b]Crafting Slots[/b]

[list]
[*] There are 2-5 crafting slots for a recipe, depending on rarity.
[*] Each Crafting Slot has a Material Type and a quantity – e.g. For a common item, the recipe can have the following slots: 2x Metal and 3x Fabric
[*] For an item to be crafted, all required slots must be completed.
[*] An item will be successfully crafted using any materials of the type and quantity specified in the Recipe: Metals, Fabrics or Crystals.
[*] Each material provides a different stat allowing the player to experiment and create different items starting from the same recipe.
[*] Completing all Crafting Slots with the appropriate materials results in 100% chance to craft that item.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/4e785616fbdb38a5506b6acb1170b4475b5d26bb.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/66c37ee0da0453e596ee0560f2427c2842286b56.jpg[/img]

[b]Unstable Slot[/b]
This is the true wildcard of the crafting system, allowing the player greater freedom in crafting but bringing along greater risk in the crafting process.

[list]
[*] Additional to the normal Crafting Slots, that provide 100% chance to craft the item, all recipes also include an unstable slot.
[*] This unstable slot is completely optional, filling it is not required to craft an item.
[*] The Unstable Slot is the only slot where Fragments can be placed, a special type of crafting material, that provide enhanced stats.
[*] The Unstable Slot allows the player to craft more powerful items but with the added risk of the item’s chance to be successfully crafted decreasing.
[*] For each item placed in the Unstable Slot, the chance to craft decreases by 15% and the item durability decreases by 3%.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/a421b46660a4e3ea7080776314f076e900c59088.jpg[/img]
 
[b]The Blacksmith:[/b]
Being part of the Outpost facilities, crafting is accessible through the Blacksmith and uses the Outpost inventory, where all the materials accumulated during the player’s adventures are located.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/5af1e4df439b0880850bab34704c96b0b539cfcf.png[/img]
 
As with most of the buildings in the Outpost, the Blacksmith can be upgraded, providing access to more recipes or other bonuses. More about the Outpost and the upgrade system in a future Devlog.

With crafting is almost in testing phase, Alchemy and Cooking are already in development and they will be the subject of our next Devlog, followed by the other systems that make up the Outpost. 




If you want to join the conversation, you can join our Discord:
 
[url=discord.zoriagame.com][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37113177/19d7859b4b198674e9889887d5720324d8ae3470.jpg[/img]
[/url]

notes.title: Devlog: Stats
notes.content:
Greetings adventurers of Zoria,

We’ve had a busy couple of months with the release of the Prologue and the Steam Summer Festival, going through all the awesome feedback we have received from you and updating and improving the Prologue based on that feedback.
With Prologue update 0.3.5 launched and all that behind us now, we are moving towards finalizing development for the features that are still missing and adding content for the game.

For today’s Devlog we will make an in-depth presentation of the updated stats system and its influence on skills and items in the game. We will not be discussing exact numbers since game balance is still ongoing and many of these numbers will probably be adjusted several times before release, but the workings of the system remain in place.

First thing to mention, we are renaming some stats that proved to be confusing for a lot of players to be more in-line with classic RPG players expectations.
[list]
[*] [b]Mastery[/b] becomes [b]Strength[/b]
[*] [b]Prowess[/b] is now more properly named [b]Agility[/b]
[*] [b]Speed[/b] is now [b]Initiative[/b], to better illustrate its role in the combat queue.
[/list]

Together with the new Stats we are introducing several new concepts:
[list]
[*] [b]Melee Attack Power[/b]
[*] [b]Ranged Attack Power [/b]
[*] [b]Spell Power [/b]
[*] [b]Block Power[/b]
[/list]

Every ability’s power is influenced by one of these 3 values, and each of these values is directly influenced by a Main Stat.

Block power only applies to characters wearing a shield and mitigates a percentage of the damage received depending on the Block Power of that character. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35921056/4d4071ef9e10513a3daad7d9d233f8fe0bbdd4ea.png[/img]

With all this said, character stats now look like this:

[b]Main Stats[/b]

These stats directly influence the character’s various attributes (health, damage) and the power of a character’s individual abilities.
[list]
[*] [b]Stamina:[/b] directly affects the character’s health. Especially important early game and the single greatest contributor to player survivability.
[*] [b]Strength:[/b] especially important for melee characters, directly affects Melee Attack Power and increases the Energy pool for Lancer class and Captain. Also increases block power for characters wearing a Shield.
[*] [b]Agility:[/b] increases Ranged Attack Power for Ranger. Increases Melee Attack Power for Thief. Increases Melee Attack Power for Lancer, Kingsman, Battle Cleric and Captain, to a smaller degree. Increases Energy pool for Ranger, Thief, Kingsman. Increases Crit Chance with values depending on class. Increases Armor.
[*] [b]Intellect:[/b] Increases Spell Power.  Increases Magic Armor. Increases Crit Chance for magic abilities. Increases Mana pool for Wizard, Necromancer, Priest, Battle Cleric, Bard.
[*] [b]Armor:[/b] reduces the amount of damage received from physical abilities and effects.
[*] [b]Magic Armor:[/b] reduces the amount of damage received from magic abilities and effects.
[/list]

[b]Secondary Stats:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Initiative:[/b] it influences the character’s place in the combat queue at the start of the combat as well as the place it will be placed in the queue once that character’s turn is finished. A character with a high Initiative value will be placed higher in the combat queue, once its turn is completed, than a character with a low Initiative value. 
[*] [b]Hit Chance:[/b] chance to hit with an ability. Is directly influenced by level difference between the character and the enemy. The higher the level of an enemy compared to the character, the lower the Hit Chance.
[*] [b]Crit Chance:[/b] Critical chance is influenced by the dominant stat for that class – Agility or Intellect.
[/list]

[b]Elemental Resistances:[/b]

All magic effects belong to a type of elemental magic. 
[list]
[*] [b]Fire Magic[/b]
[*] [b]Water Magic[/b]
[*] [b]Nature Magic[/b]
[*] [b]Arcane Magic[/b]
[*] [b]Death Magic[/b]
[*] [b]Light Magic[/b]
[/list]

Light and Death Magic are in direct opposition, with Death Magic wielders being especially weak to Light Magic and Light Magic wielders especially weak to Death Magic abilities.
Enemies weak to Fire Magic are also equally weak to physical Fire effects, like the Fire Arrow Ranger ability.
Elemental resistances mitigate a percent of the incoming damage from that specific element. Gear pieces with elemental resistance have values representing their elemental resistance. These values translate to different percentages of elemental resistance, depending on level, making a low-level gear piece more effective in elemental protection for the appropriate level character.



[b]Effects:[/b]

These effects are placed on the character by various abilities and can be temporary (only during combat) or permanent (must be removed either by resting, using a potion or in the Outpost). Each effect influences the player’s stats differently:

[list]
[*] [b]Sunder:[/b] can be applied by physical abilities. Decreases the player Armor and can stack multiple effects.
[*] [b]Wound:[/b] can be applied by physical abilities. Decreases the player [b]Initiative[/b] while active.
[*] [b]Bleed:[/b] can be applied by physical abilities. Deals damage over time to the character until removed.
[*] [b]Stun:[/b] can be applied by any kind of abilities. Locks the character in the current position in the combat queue for its duration.
[*] [b]Poison:[/b] can be applied by Nature abilities. Decreases [b]Hit Chance[/b].
[*] [b]Disease:[/b] can be applied by Nature abilities. Decreases [b]Agility[/b] and [b]Intellect[/b].
[*] [b]Curse:[/b] can be applied by Death abilities. Decreases [b]Strength[/b] and [b]Magic Armor[/b].
[/list]

These effects do not show on the Character Stat sheet but in the abilities description for each ability that places a certain effect. Some enemies can be immune to certain types of effects, making the abilities that place those effects less effective. This immunity will be shown in the Compendium entry for each enemy.

[b]Stats influence on abilities:[/b]
The power of each ability of a certain class is affected by a main stat. Because of this, different builds for a class can benefit from a different main stat.

As an example, below some of the Kingsman’s abilities and the stats affecting their power:
[list]
[*] [b]Strength:[/b] Basic Attack, Vanquish thy Foe, Avenger Strike, Bash of Wrath
[*] [b]Agility:[/b] Shield Wall, King's Resolve, Deflect, Hold the Line, Avatar of Protection
[*] [b]Intellect:[/b] Magic Absorption, King's Fire
[/list]


[b]Fatigue:[/b] is a special stat, central to the Fatigue and Outpost recovery mechanic. We will introduce more details on this mechanic in a dedicated post, at a later date.

Together with the Stats update we are also introducing new stats to armor and weapons.

[b]Durability:[/b] all weapons and armor now have a certain durability that decreases with each combat. Once a gear item’s durability reaches 0, that item is no longer usable and provides no contribution to the character’s stats.

[b]Armor Types:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Light Armor:[/b] worn by Wizard, Necromancer and Priest classes.
[*] [b]Medium Armor:[/b] worn by Ranger, Thief, Bard classes and the Captain.
[*] [b]Hardened Armor:[/b] worn by the Ranger, Kingsman, Lancer, Battle Cleric classes and the Captain.
[*] [b]Heavy Armor:[/b] worn by the Kingsman and Lancer classes.
[/list]

[b]Weapon Damage and Spell Damage:[/b]
[list]
[*] All weapons now have a weapon damage stat. This damage is added to the base attack of the character using that weapon.
[*] Specific caster weapons, like the staff, have a Spell Damage stat instead of Weapon Damage.
[/list]

There are any more changes coming to Armor and Weapons, but we will detail those systems in our next Developer Log, that will focus on gear and the Crafting System.
